newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN CONFIDENT OF BEATING RIVALS INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN CONFIDENT OF BEATING RIVALS INDIA.

text.p: Pakistan, looking to win the Asia Cup for the first time, are confident they can beat fierce rivals India on Sunday and book a place in the final against Sri Lanka.
"We have never won the Asia Cup and this is foremost in our minds," Pakistan coach Haroon Rashid said.
"In view of our batting strength and various bowling combinations and variety, I think on paper you could say that we have the edge over India."
Whoever win's Sunday's match at Colombo's Singhalese Sports Club will qualify to meet the world champions in the final on July 26.
"If you take our first six batsmen, they have so many one-day centuries and fifties against their names," added Haroon. "As far as our batting is concerned, we are superior to India."
India know they have a tough task on their hands. Skipper Sachin Tendulkar said he hoped former captain Mohammad Azharuddin would play a big innings.
"Azhar's role will be important. I hope he will bat as he did against Sri Lanka. He is the kind of batsman, when he gets going, he is very hard to stop," said Tendulkar.
Azharuddin's innings of 81 not out was one of the few high points for India in their defeat by Sri Lanka on Friday.

"Our bowling needs to be tightened up a little more because we bowled quite a lot of wide balls and no balls, and some loose deliveries. We would, like to minimise that as much as possible," Tendulkar said.
"Against Pakistan, it is always a big game. I would like to play better than we did against Sri Lanka."
To raise their form, the Indian captain said the team was trying out a new policy of dining together and trying to encourage each other.
"You cannot go back into the rooms and do it. If we sit together and spend time together, it helps a lot," he said.
India go into the game as underdogs having lost 33 of 51 head-to-head clashes with their arch rivals.

India (from): Sachin Tendulkar, (captain), Saurav Ganguly, Rahul Dravid, Mohammad Azharuddin, Robin Singh, Saba Karim, Ajay Jadega, Anil Kumble, Venkatesh Prasad, Abey Kuruwila, Noel David, Navjot Sidhu, Nilesh Kulkarni, Debasish Mohanty.

Pakistan (from): Rameez Raja (captain), Saeed Anwar, Aamir Sohail, Inzamam-ul-Haq, Salim Malik, Shahid Afridi, Moin Khan, Saqlain Mushtaq, Aaqib Javed, Arshad Khan, Kabir Khan, Hasan Raza, Shahid Nazir, Mohammad Hussain.
